main_text.p: Bullæus de tribus Gener. jur. Præ-cept.Bac-chov.vo-lum.i.ad Treutl. disp. 32. p. 1282. Hieron. Cagnolds ad l. 51. D. de Reg. jur. Covarr. in c, pec-catum, de Reg. jur. in 6. part. 2. relect. §. 3. n.4. Gomes. Var.ref. tom.3. c. 2.n.9. Franci-scus Viv. Comm. Opinion. in v. de-fendere offensum num. 3. Bronch. ad l. 51. tamen quemcunque absolute ad defensionem alterius homi-nis in periculo constituti, obligari. Ita tantum ut id jure possit, etiam occidendo iniquum aggressorem.

Atque haec nostra sententia etiam praestantissimis placuit jurisconsultis, & in tantum dis-plicuit opinio Bartoli, ut Baldus dixerit, eum propter hanc in inferno cruciari. Estque Baldi sententia in tantum vera, ut etiam is, qui proximi defensionem neglectui habuit, arbitrio judicis sit puniendus. Leges certe civiles, multis in locis hanc comprobant opinionem. Non tantum enim inter parentes & liberos, aliosque sanguinis vinculo nobis junctos, natura constituit aliquod vinculum, verum etiam aliquam cognationem, & so-ciationem inter omnes homines. page.notes: The column is the only visible text; its main text is cut off, so the side is inferred from the position of the column. Doubtful readings: "Cagnolds" (possibly Cagnoldus), "Bac-chov" (the join and the word are unclear), "in c," (possibly "in c."). Printed long s is given as plain s (for example "Gomes" for the form that looks like "Gomef"). The column is one continuous run of lines, so it is set as one note; it may hold several separate notes, which cannot be told apart in this part. The first line of the page is the end of a sentence from the previous page. The printed line numbers and catchword were read as shown; the page number is partly cut off, so its first digit is uncertain.
